title: Australia Bans AI-Made Songs from Music Charts
paragraphs: Australia's music industry has banned songs that are made completely by artificial intelligence from its official music charts.

The Australian Recording Industry Association (ARIA), which runs the country's official charts, announced the new rules in August 2026. They took effect at the end of August. Under the rules, a song can only appear on the charts if humans wrote it and performed the main vocals and the main instruments. Songs that use AI only as a helping tool can still be included. However, the AI tools used must be legal. AI-generated music also cannot win ARIA Awards, the country's most famous music awards.

The decision followed a controversy over a new version of Madonna's famous song "Like a Prayer." An Australian producer made the song using AI-generated vocals and drums. It became very popular with listeners. It spent 16 weeks in the Australian top 20 and reached number two on the ARIA singles chart in May.
Some streaming music also seems to have been made with AI tools that were trained on artists' work without permission.

Annabelle Herd, the chief executive of ARIA, said the changes show that the organization wants to promote the human nature of making music. She also said that a chart that rewards unlicensed AI music would harm the industry.

Alexis Weaver, a composer and lecturer at the Sydney Conservatorium of Music, said the debate was very emotional for many musicians. She called ARIA's decision a positive step that values human creativity. However, she also said that musicians can still use AI while making the main creative decisions themselves.
The new rules follow principles released in July by an international music industry organization, which said songs must be "substantially human made."
